title: Indefinite Articles: A vs. An
description: Master the rules of sound-based indefinite articles (a vs an) before singular countable nouns.
objectives: Distinguish between consonant sounds and vowel sounds in English pronunciation
Use 'a' before consonant sounds and 'an' before vowel sounds correctly
Identify tricky sound-based words like 'an hour', 'a university', and 'an honest person'

sections.title: The Sound Rule for A vs. An
sections.content:
In English, **a** and **an** are indefinite articles. We use them **only before singular countable nouns** when mentioning something general or for the first time.

### The Cardinal Rule
The choice between **a** and **an** is determined by **SOUND**, not by the written letter:
- Use **a** before a **consonant sound** (e.g. /b/, /d/, /k/, /j/).
- Use **an** before a **vowel sound** (e.g. /Ã¦/, /e/, /Éª/, /É’/, /ÊŒ/, /aÊŠ/).

callouts.title: Say It Out Loud
callouts.text: If your tongue or lips catch when saying the word, it's a consonant sound (use 'a'). If your throat is open and vowels flow smoothly, use 'an' to create a smooth bridge.

callouts.title: Never Use with Plural or Uncountable Nouns
callouts.text: Never say 'a books' or 'a water'. Articles 'a' and 'an' literally mean 'one'!

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: Use 'a' and 'an' ONLY with singular countable nouns.
Choose 'a' before consonant SOUNDS (a cat, a doctor, a university).
Choose 'an' before vowel SOUNDS (an apple, an egg, an hour).
Remember silent 'h' words take 'an' (an hour, an honest man).
Remember 'u' words that sound like 'yoo' take 'a' (a university, a unique style).
